facts.statement: The genus Cathayopterus was described in 2006 by Wang Xiaolin and Zhou Zhonghe.
facts.quote: The type species is C. grabaui, described in 2006 by Wang Xiaolin and Zhou Zhonghe.

facts.statement: The name Cathayopterus means "China wing", derived from the historical name Cathay for China.
facts.quote: The name means "China wing", using the word "Cathay" as an old alternative name for China.

facts.statement: Cathayopterus belongs to the Ctenochasmatidae, a group of pterosaurs that mostly fed by filtering.
facts.quote: It is a member of the Ctenochasmatidae, a clade of mostly filter feeding pterosaurs from the Jurassic and early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The only known fossil is a skull showing teeth that splay outwards at the tip of the snout.
facts.quote: Cathayopterus is only known from a skull (IVPP V13756) preserved in dorsal view, which shows teeth splaying outwards at the tip of the rostrum, similar to Ctenochasma.

facts.statement: The known skull fossil is incomplete and damaged on the left side.
facts.quote: The skull is incomplete, with the left side being damaged.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Cathayopterus as a basal member of the family Ctenochasmatidae.
facts.quote: They recovered Cathayopterus as a basal member of the family Ctenochasmatidae.

facts.statement: Cathayopterus lived during the Early Cretaceous in the Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Cathayopterus is an extinct genus of ctenochasmatid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous-age Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: Cathayopterus was likely a filter feeder, similar to other members of its family.
facts.quote: Cathayopterus was likely a filter feeder, just like other ctenochasmatid pterosaurs.

facts.statement: Cathayopterus likely roamed around waterways to feed.
facts.quote: It likely roamed around waterways to feed.

facts.statement: Cathayopterus lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago during the Barremian to Aptian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: Cathayopterus is classified within the suborder Pterodactyloidea.
Cathayopterus is classified in the family Ctenochasmatidae.
The placement of Cathayopterus in the Ctenochasmatidae was confirmed by a cladistic analysis by Lü Junchang in 2007.
facts.quote: Wang coloca la especie en el Ctenochasmatidae, que fue confirmado por un análisis cladístico de Lü Junchang en 2007.

facts.statement: According to Wang, Cathayopterus consumed small invertebrates from the water, feeding by filtration like Ctenochasma and Pterodaustro.
facts.quote: De acuerdo a Wang, Cathayopterus es un miembro de los pterosaurios que se alimentaban por filtración, consumiendo pequeños investrebrados del agua como Ctenochasma y Pterodaustro.
